candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — transdermal medication administration and client teaching
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — clonidine transdermal administration
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the labeled application site and replacement interval for clonidine transdermal systems.

options.A: Apply the patch over broken or irritated skin to increase absorption.
options.B: Replace the patch every day because the dose lasts only 24 hours.
options.C: Apply it to a hairless area of intact skin and replace it every 7 days, rotating sites.
options.D: Cut the patch into smaller pieces whenever a lower dose is desired.

candidate.rationale: Clonidine transdermal system labeling directs application once every 7 days to a hairless area of intact skin on the upper outer arm or chest, with each new application placed at a different site. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Apply clonidine transdermal system once every 7 days to a hairless area of intact skin and rotate application sites.
candidate.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a client using a clonidine transdermal system?
